050/**
051 * OpModeRobot implements the opmode-based robot program framework.
052 *
053 * <p>The OpModeRobot class is intended to be subclassed by a user creating a robot program.
054 *
055 * <p>Classes annotated with {@link Autonomous}, {@link Teleop}, and {@link Utility} in the same
056 * package or subpackages as the user's subclass are automatically registered as autonomous, teleop,
057 * and utility opmodes respectively.
058 *
059 * <p>Opmodes are constructed when selected on the driver station. While selected and disabled,
060 * {@link PeriodicOpMode#disabledPeriodic()} is called. When enabled, {@link PeriodicOpMode#start()}
061 * is called once and {@link PeriodicOpMode#periodic()} runs at the rate from {@link #getPeriod()}.
062 * On disable or mode switch while enabled, {@link PeriodicOpMode#end()} is called asynchronously
063 * and the opmode is then closed and discarded. When no opmode is selected, {@link #nonePeriodic()}
064 * is called. {@link #driverStationConnected()} is called once when the DS first connects.
065 *
066 * <p>Every period, the robot's loop function runs first, calling these in order:
067 *
068 * <ol>
069 *   <li>{@link #disabledPeriodic()}, only while disabled
070 *   <li>{@link PeriodicOpMode#disabledPeriodic()} of the selected opmode, only while disabled
071 *   <li>{@link #nonePeriodic()}, only when no opmode is selected
072 *   <li>{@link #robotPeriodic()}
073 *   <li>{@link #simulationPeriodic()}, only in simulation
074 * </ol>
075 *
076 * <p>Then, while enabled, {@link PeriodicOpMode#periodic()} runs. Both are scheduled on the same
077 * period, and the loop function was registered first, so {@link #robotPeriodic()} and {@link
078 * #simulationPeriodic()} always run before {@link PeriodicOpMode#periodic()} in a given period.
079 * Additional callbacks from {@link #addPeriodic} or the opmode run on their own schedules.
080 *
081 * <p>One exception to the list above: if an opmode is selected while the robot is already enabled,
082 * its {@code disabledPeriodic()} is called once, right after construction and before {@code
083 * start()}, even though the robot is not disabled. That call happens before {@link
084 * #robotPeriodic()} in that loop.
085 */
086public abstract class OpModeRobot extends RobotBase {
087  private final ControlWord m_word = new ControlWord();
088

090

107  private final Set<Callback> m_activeOpModeCallbacks = new HashSet<>();
108  private final Watchdog m_watchdog;
109  private final Alert m_loopOverrunAlert;
110  private final Watchdog m_opModeWatchdog;
111  private final Alert m_opModePeriodicOverrunAlert;

113  private static void reportAddOpModeError(Class<?> cls, String message) {
114    DriverStationErrors.reportError(
115        "Error adding OpMode " + cls.getSimpleName() + ": " + message, false);
116  }

118  /**
119   * Find a public constructor to instantiate the opmode. This constructor can have up to 2
120   * parameters. The first parameter (if present) must be assignable from this.getClass(). The
121   * second parameter (if present) must be assignable from DriverStationBase. If multiple, first
122   * sort by most parameters, then by most specific first, then by most specific second.
123   */
124  private <T> Optional<ConstructorMatch<T>> findOpModeConstructor(Class<T> cls) {
125    Optional<ConstructorMatch<T>> ctor;
126
127    // try 1-parameter constructor with RobotBase parameter
128    ctor = ConstructorMatch.findBestConstructor(cls, getClass());
129    if (ctor.isPresent()) {
130      return ctor;
131    }
132
133    // try no-parameter constructor
134    ctor = ConstructorMatch.findBestConstructor(cls);
135    return ctor;
136  }
137
138  private <T extends OpMode> T constructOpModeClass(Class<T> cls) {
139    Optional<ConstructorMatch<T>> constructor = findOpModeConstructor(cls);
140    if (constructor.isEmpty()) {
141      DriverStationErrors.reportError(
142          "No suitable constructor to instantiate OpMode " + cls.getSimpleName(), true);
143      return null;
144    }
145    try {
146      return constructor.get().newInstance(this);
147    } catch (ReflectiveOperationException e) {
148      throw new RuntimeException(
149          "Could not instantiate OpMode " + cls.getSimpleName(), e.getCause());
150    }
151  }
152
153  private void checkOpModeClass(Class<?> cls) {
154    // the class must be a subclass of OpMode
155    if (!OpMode.class.isAssignableFrom(cls)) {
156      throw new IllegalArgumentException("not a subclass of OpMode");
157    }
158    int modifiers = cls.getModifiers();
159    // it cannot be abstract
160    if (Modifier.isAbstract(modifiers)) {
161      throw new IllegalArgumentException("is abstract");
162    }
163    // it must be public
164    if (!Modifier.isPublic(modifiers)) {
165      throw new IllegalArgumentException("not public");
166    }
167    // it must not be a non-static inner class
168    if (cls.getEnclosingClass() != null && !Modifier.isStatic(modifiers)) {
169      throw new IllegalArgumentException("is a non-static inner class");
170    }
171    // it must have a public no-arg constructor or a public constructor that accepts this class
172    // (or a superclass/interface) as an argument
173    if (findOpModeConstructor(cls).isEmpty()) {
174      throw new IllegalArgumentException(
175          "missing public no-arg constructor or constructor accepting "
176              + getClass().getSimpleName());
177    }
178  }

180  /**

182   * publishOpModes() to make the added mode visible to the driver station.
183   *
184   * @param mode robot mode
185   * @param name name of the operating mode
186   * @param group group of the operating mode
187   * @param description description of the operating mode
188   * @param textColor text color, or null for default
189   * @param backgroundColor background color, or null for default
190   * @param factory factory function to create the opmode
191   * @throws IllegalArgumentException if class does not meet criteria
192   */
193  public void addOpMode(
194      RobotMode mode,
195      String name,
196      String group,
197      String description,
198      Color textColor,
199      Color backgroundColor,
200      Supplier<OpMode> factory) {
201    long id = RobotState.addOpMode(mode, name, group, description, textColor, backgroundColor);

335  private void addOpModeClassImpl(
336      Class<? extends OpMode> cls,
337      RobotMode mode,
338      String name,
339      String group,
340      String description,
341      String textColor,
342      String backgroundColor) {
343    if (name == null || name.isBlank()) {
344      name = cls.getSimpleName();
345    }
346    Color tColor = textColor.isBlank() ? null : Color.fromString(textColor);
347    Color bColor = backgroundColor.isBlank() ? null : Color.fromString(backgroundColor);
348    long id = RobotState.addOpMode(mode, name, group, description, tColor, bColor);
349    m_opModes.put(id, new OpModeFactory(name, () -> constructOpModeClass(cls)));
350  }
351
352  private void addAnnotatedOpModeImpl(
353      Class<? extends OpMode> cls, Autonomous auto, Teleop teleop, Utility utility) {
354    checkOpModeClass(cls);
355
356    // add an opmode for each annotation
357    if (auto != null) {
358      addOpModeClassImpl(
359          cls,
360          RobotMode.AUTONOMOUS,
361          auto.name(),
362          auto.group(),
363          auto.description(),
364          auto.textColor(),
365          auto.backgroundColor());
366    }
367    if (teleop != null) {
368      addOpModeClassImpl(
369          cls,
370          RobotMode.TELEOPERATED,
371          teleop.name(),
372          teleop.group(),
373          teleop.description(),
374          teleop.textColor(),
375          teleop.backgroundColor());
376    }
377    if (utility != null) {
378      addOpModeClassImpl(
379          cls,
380          RobotMode.UTILITY,
381          utility.name(),
382          utility.group(),
383          utility.description(),
384          utility.textColor(),
385          utility.backgroundColor());
386    }
387  }

389  /**
390   * Adds an opmode for an opmode class annotated with {@link Autonomous}, {@link Teleop}, or {@link
391   * Utility}. The class must be a public, non-abstract subclass of OpMode with a public constructor
392   * that either takes no arguments or accepts a single argument assignable from this robot class
393   * type (if multiple match, the most specific parameter type is used). It's necessary to call
394   * publishOpModes() to make the added mode visible to the driver station.
395   *
396   * @param cls class to add
397   * @throws IllegalArgumentException if class does not meet criteria
398   */
399  public void addAnnotatedOpMode(Class<? extends OpMode> cls) {
400    Autonomous auto = cls.getAnnotation(Autonomous.class);
401    Teleop teleop = cls.getAnnotation(Teleop.class);
402    Utility utility = cls.getAnnotation(Utility.class);
403    if (auto == null && teleop == null && utility == null) {
404      throw new IllegalArgumentException("must be annotated with Autonomous, Teleop, or Utility");
405    }
406    addAnnotatedOpModeImpl(cls, auto, teleop, utility);
407  }
408
409  private void addAnnotatedOpModeClass(String name) {
410    // trim ".class" from end
411    String className = name.replace('/', '.').substring(0, name.length() - 6);
412    Class<? extends OpMode> cls;
413    try {
414      cls =
415          Class.forName(className, false, Thread.currentThread().getContextClassLoader())
416              .asSubclass(OpMode.class);
417    } catch (ClassNotFoundException | ClassCastException e) {
418      return;
419    }
420    Autonomous auto = cls.getAnnotation(Autonomous.class);
421    Teleop teleop = cls.getAnnotation(Teleop.class);
422    Utility utility = cls.getAnnotation(Utility.class);
423    if (auto == null && teleop == null && utility == null) {
424      return;
425    }
426    try {
427      addAnnotatedOpModeImpl(cls, auto, teleop, utility);
428    } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
429      reportAddOpModeError(cls, e.getMessage());
430    }
431  }
432
433  private void addAnnotatedOpModeClassesDir(File root, File dir, String packagePath) {
434    File[] files = dir.listFiles();
435    if (files == null) {
436      return;
437    }
438    for (File file : files) {
439      if (file.isDirectory()) {
440        addAnnotatedOpModeClassesDir(root, file, packagePath);
441      } else if (file.getName().endsWith(".class")) {
442        String relPath = root.toPath().relativize(file.toPath()).toString().replace('\\', '/');
443        addAnnotatedOpModeClass(packagePath + "." + relPath);
444      }
445    }
446  }
447
448  /**
449   * Scans for classes in the specified package and all nested packages that are annotated with
450   * {@link Autonomous}, {@link Teleop}, or {@link Utility} and registers them. It's necessary to
451   * call publishOpModes() to make the added modes visible to the driver station.
452   *
453   * @param pkg package to scan
454   */
455  public void addAnnotatedOpModeClasses(Package pkg) {
456    String packageName = pkg.getName();
457    String packagePath = packageName.replace('.', '/');
458    ClassLoader classLoader = Thread.currentThread().getContextClassLoader();
459
460    try {
461      Enumeration<URL> resources = classLoader.getResources(packagePath);
462      while (resources.hasMoreElements()) {
463        URL resource = resources.nextElement();
464        if ("jar".equals(resource.getProtocol())) {
465          var connection = resource.openConnection();
466          if (!(connection instanceof JarURLConnection jarConnection)) {
467            DriverStationErrors.reportError(
468                "Error scanning OpModes from "
469                    + resource
470                    + ": expected JarURLConnection, got "
471                    + connection.getClass().getSimpleName(),
472                false);
473            continue;
474          }
475          jarConnection.setUseCaches(false);
476          try (JarFile jar = jarConnection.getJarFile()) {
477            Enumeration<JarEntry> entries = jar.entries();
478            while (entries.hasMoreElements()) {
479              String name = entries.nextElement().getName();
480              if (!name.startsWith(packagePath) || !name.endsWith(".class")) {
481                continue;
482              }
483              addAnnotatedOpModeClass(name);
484            }
485          }
486        } else if ("file".equals(resource.getProtocol())) {
487          // Handle .class files in directories
488          File dir = new File(resource.toURI());
489          if (dir.exists() && dir.isDirectory()) {
490            addAnnotatedOpModeClassesDir(dir, dir, packagePath);
491          }
492        }
493      }
494    } catch (IOException | URISyntaxException e) {
495      e.printStackTrace();
496    }
497  }

499  /**
500   * Removes an operating mode option. It's necessary to call publishOpModes() to make the removed
501   * mode no longer visible to the driver station.
502   *
503   * @param mode robot mode
504   * @param name name of the operating mode
505   */
506  public void removeOpMode(RobotMode mode, String name) {

524  /** Default loop period. */
525  public static final double DEFAULT_PERIOD = 0.02;
526
527  /** Constructor with default period. */
528  @SuppressWarnings("this-escape")
529  public OpModeRobot() {
530    this(DEFAULT_PERIOD);
531  }
532
533  /**
534   * Constructor with specified period.
535   *
536   * @param period the period at which to run the robot and opmode periodic callbacks.
537   */
538  @SuppressWarnings("this-escape")
539  public OpModeRobot(double period) {
540    m_period = period;
541
542    // Create our own notifier and callback queue (match C++)
543    m_notifier = NotifierJNI.createNotifier();
544    NotifierJNI.setNotifierName(m_notifier, "OpModeRobot");
545
546    m_startTimeNs = RobotController.getMonotonicTime();
547
548    m_loopOverrunAlert =
549        new Alert(
550            "opmoderobot-loop-overrun",
551            "Loop time of " + m_period + "s overrun",
552            Alert.Level.MEDIUM);
553    m_watchdog = new Watchdog(Seconds.of(m_period), () -> m_loopOverrunAlert.set(true));
554    m_opModePeriodicOverrunAlert =
555        new Alert(
556            "opmode-periodic-overrun",
557            "OpMode periodic() time of " + m_period + "s overrun",
558            Alert.Level.MEDIUM);
559    m_opModeWatchdog =
560        new Watchdog(Seconds.of(m_period), () -> m_opModePeriodicOverrunAlert.set(true));
561
562    // Add LoopFunc as periodic callback (match C++)
563    addPeriodic(this::loopFunc, period);
564
565    // Scan for annotated opmode classes within the derived class's package and subpackages
566    addAnnotatedOpModeClasses(getClass().getPackage());
567    RobotState.publishOpModes();
568
569    UsageReporting.reportUsage("Framework", "OpModeRobot");
570  }

590  /**
591   * Add a callback to run at a specific period.
592   *
593   * <p>This callback will be registered with the framework immediately when this method is called
594   * and will begin executing as soon as it is registered.
595   *
596   * @param callback The callback to run.
597   * @param period The period at which to run the callback in seconds.
598   */
599  public final void addPeriodic(Runnable callback, double period) {
600    addPeriodic(callback, period, 0);
601  }
602
603  /**
604   * Add a callback to run at a specific period with a starting time offset.
605   *
606   * <p>This callback will be registered with the framework immediately when this method is called
607   * and will begin executing as soon as it is registered.
608   *
609   * @param callback The callback to run.
610   * @param period The period at which to run the callback in seconds.
611   * @param offset The offset from the common starting time in seconds. This is useful for
612   *     scheduling a callback in a different timeslot relative to OpModeRobot.
613   */
614  public final void addPeriodic(Runnable callback, double period, double offset) {
615    m_callbacks.add(callback, m_startTimeNs, period, offset);
616  }

623  public double getPeriod() {
624    return m_period;

677  /**
678   * Return the system clock time in nanoseconds for the start of the current periodic loop. This is
679   * in the same time base as Timer.getMonotonicTimestamp(), but is stable through a loop. It is
680   * updated at the beginning of every periodic callback (including the normal periodic loop).
681   *
682   * @return Robot running time in nanoseconds, as of the start of the current periodic function.
683   */
684  public long getLoopStartTime() {
685    return m_callbacks.getLoopStartTime();

687
688  /** Main robot loop function. Handles disabled state logic and opmode management. */
689  private void loopFunc() {
690    DriverStationBackend.refreshData();
691
692    // Get current enabled state and opmode
693    DriverStationBackend.refreshControlWordFromCache(m_word);
694    m_watchdog.reset();
695    final boolean enabled = m_word.isEnabled();
696    // Treat disabled as unknown
697    final RobotMode mode = enabled ? m_word.getRobotMode() : RobotMode.UNKNOWN;
698    long modeId = m_word.isDSAttached() ? m_word.getOpModeId() : 0;
699
700    boolean modeChanged = modeId != m_lastModeId;
701    m_lastModeId = modeId;
702
703    if (!m_calledDriverStationConnected && m_word.isDSAttached()) {
704      m_calledDriverStationConnected = true;
705      driverStationConnected();
706    }
707
708    // Handle opmode changes: tear down the old opmode if the selection changed
709    if (modeChanged && m_currentOpMode != null) {
710      endCurrentOpMode();
711    }
712
713    // Set up new opmode
714    if (modeId != 0 && m_currentOpMode == null && modeChanged) {
715      OpModeFactory factory = m_opModes.get(modeId);
716      if (factory != null) {
717        m_currentOpModeName = factory.name();
718        System.out.println("********** Creating OpMode " + m_currentOpModeName + " **********");
719        m_currentOpMode = factory.supplier().get();
720        if (m_currentOpMode != null) {
721          // Register the opmode's additional periodic callbacks immediately on creation
722          m_activeOpModeCallbacks.addAll(m_currentOpMode.getCallbacks());
723          m_callbacks.addAll(m_activeOpModeCallbacks);
724
725          // extra DisabledPeriodic call
726          if (enabled) {
727            m_currentOpMode.disabledPeriodic();
728            m_watchdog.addEpoch("OpMode::DisabledPeriodic()");
729          }
730        }
731      } else {
732        DriverStationErrors.reportError("No OpMode found for mode " + modeId, false);
733      }
734    }
735
736    // If mode changed, call disabled exit and entry functions
737    if (m_lastMode != mode) {
738      if (m_lastMode == RobotMode.UNKNOWN) {
739        // Transitioning out of disabled
740        disabledExit();
741      }
742      if (mode == RobotMode.UNKNOWN) {
743        // Transitioning to disabled. Only tear down an opmode that was actually
744        // running; a freshly selected opmode entering its disabled phase must
745        // persist so it can be started on the next enable.
746        if (m_currentOpMode != null && m_currentOpModePeriodic != null) {
747          endCurrentOpMode();
748          m_lastModeId = -1; // force recreate next loop
749        }
750        disabledInit();
751        m_watchdog.addEpoch("disabledInit()");
752      }
753      m_lastMode = mode;
754    }
755
756    // Start the opmode if enabled and not already started. This single check
757    // covers both the disabled->enabled transition and an opmode constructed
758    // while the robot is already enabled.
759    if (enabled && m_currentOpMode != null && m_currentOpModePeriodic == null) {
760      startCurrentOpMode();
761    }
762
763    // Call periodic functions based on current state
764    DriverStationJNI.observeUserProgram(m_word.getNative());
765    if (!enabled) {
766      disabledPeriodic();
767      m_watchdog.addEpoch("disabledPeriodic()");
768
769      // Call opmode disabledPeriodic if we have one
770      if (m_currentOpMode != null) {
771        m_currentOpMode.disabledPeriodic();
772        m_watchdog.addEpoch("opMode.disabledPeriodic()");
773      }
774    }
775
776    // Call nonePeriodic when no opmode is selected
777    if (modeId == 0) {
778      nonePeriodic();
779      m_watchdog.addEpoch("nonePeriodic()");
780    }
781
782    // Always call robotPeriodic
783    robotPeriodic();
784    m_watchdog.addEpoch("robotPeriodic()");
785
786    TunableRegistry.update();
787    m_watchdog.addEpoch("TunableRegistry.update()");
788
789    // Call simulationPeriodic if in simulation
790    if (isSimulation()) {
791      HAL.simPeriodicBefore();
792      simulationPeriodic();
793      HAL.simPeriodicAfter();
794      m_watchdog.addEpoch("simulationPeriodic()");
795    }
796
797    m_watchdog.disable();
798
799    // Flush NetworkTables
800    NetworkTableInstance.getDefault().flushLocal();
801
802    // Warn on loop time overruns, and clear the alert once the loop is back on time
803    if (m_watchdog.isExpired()) {
804      m_watchdog.printEpochs();
805    }
806    m_loopOverrunAlert.set(m_watchdog.isExpired());
807  }
808
809  private void startCurrentOpMode() {
810    if (m_currentOpMode == null || m_currentOpModePeriodic != null) {
811      return;
812    }
813
814    System.out.println("********** Starting OpMode " + m_currentOpModeName + " **********");
815
816    // Register the main opmode periodic callback
817    final OpMode opMode = m_currentOpMode;
818    m_currentOpModePeriodic =
819        m_callbacks.add(() -> runOpModePeriodic(opMode), m_startTimeNs, m_period);
820
821    m_currentOpMode.start();
822    m_watchdog.addEpoch("opMode.start()");
823  }
824
825  private void runOpModePeriodic(OpMode opMode) {
826    m_opModeWatchdog.reset();
827    opMode.periodic();
828    m_opModeWatchdog.disable();
829
830    // Alert on opmode periodic() overruns, and clear the alert once it's back on time
831    m_opModePeriodicOverrunAlert.set(m_opModeWatchdog.isExpired());
832  }
833
834  private void endCurrentOpMode() {
835    // If the opmode was started, end it and remove its main periodic callback.
836    if (m_currentOpModePeriodic != null) {
837      System.out.println("********** Ending OpMode " + m_currentOpModeName + " **********");
838
839      m_currentOpMode.end();
840      m_watchdog.addEpoch("opMode.end()");
841
842      m_callbacks.remove(m_currentOpModePeriodic);
843      m_currentOpModePeriodic = null;
844      m_opModePeriodicOverrunAlert.set(false);
845    }
846
847    // The additional getCallbacks() callbacks are registered immediately on construction (even
848    // while disabled), so always remove them regardless of whether the opmode was started.
849    m_callbacks.removeAll(m_activeOpModeCallbacks);
850    m_activeOpModeCallbacks.clear();
851
852    // regardless of whether opmode was started, close it and set to null
853    System.out.println("********** Closing OpMode " + m_currentOpModeName + " **********");
854    m_currentOpMode.close();
855    m_currentOpMode = null;
856    m_currentOpModeName = null;
857  }
858
859  /** Provide an alternate "main loop" via startCompetition(). */
860  @Override
861  public final void startCompetition() {
862    if (isSimulation()) {
863      simulationInit();
864    }
865
866    // Tell the DS that the robot is ready to be enabled
867    System.out.println("********** Robot program startup complete **********");
868    DriverStationBackend.observeUserProgramStarting();
869
870    // Loop forever, calling the callback system which handles periodic functions
871    while (true) {
872      if (!m_callbacks.runCallbacks(m_notifier)) {
873        break;
874      }
875    }
876  }
877
878  @Override
879  public void close() {
880    m_loopOverrunAlert.close();
881    m_opModePeriodicOverrunAlert.close();
882    NotifierJNI.destroyNotifier(m_notifier);
883    super.close();
884  }
885
886  /** Ends the main loop in startCompetition(). */
887  @Override
888  public final void endCompetition() {
889    NotifierJNI.destroyNotifier(m_notifier);
890  }

892  /** Prints list of epochs added so far and their times. */
893  public void printWatchdogEpochs() {
894    m_watchdog.printEpochs();
895  }
